chapter: New York 1948: Tristano and the Miles nonet
title: Rehearsals and personnel of the nonet; the scores found in Philadelphia
summary: He recalls the shifting rehearsal personnel and Kirchner describes seeing the original scores found in a warehouse.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Playing with Miles Davis: joining, sessions and the band

blocks.x: Probably in Nola’s or one of those places.

Seems like a lot. It seemed like at every rehearsal there was someone different: Nelson Boyd. On piano, I don’t remember it well; it was either John Lewis or Al Haig I think. The bass players changed: Joe Schulman. Nelson Boyd.
Well Kenny Clarke and Max Roach, basically. Different trombone players. I don’t remember it well. I don’t even remember Gunther Schuller playing on the band.
I think he was just on the last recording session, the nineteen fifty-one?
Yeah, he was on the last one. Before that it was Junior Collins or Sandy Siegelstein and they were both on Thornhill’s band, right?
Bill Barber was there pretty much all of the time?

A number of years ago I got a chance to look at the original scores for that music after they found all this stuff not only for the Birth of the Cool band but for the Miles and Gil records. They found them in a warehouse in Philadelphia about fifteen years ago and they brought them up here and a friend of mine was working at King Brand Music and called me and said “come and look at all of this stuff” so I got to look at it one afternoon. There were actually a couple of George Russell scores for that band in there that never got recorded. Do you remember those?
[Interview pauses so Konitz can adjust a lamp beside him]
